item.title: Man accused of shooting stranger during argument, Winnipeg police say
item.description: Winnipeg police say a verbal dispute between a man an a woman in a bar escalated, and the man shot the woman. Both people had left the hotel before officers arrived.

item.title: Canadians say Puerto Vallarta a ‘war zone’ amid escalating violence
item.description: Amid violence, people in Puerto Vallarta have been told to keep a low profile, follow the advice of local authorities, and monitor local and international media to stay informed.

item.title: The Curator: Handy Amazon home gadgets that *really* work
item.description: These home gadgets are the finds you didn't know you needed, but now can't live without.

item.title: The Curator: 5 unexpected cleaning secrets hiding in your home right now
item.description: Discover new ways to put your favourite cleaning staples like Dawn, Cascade and Bounce to work. Home expert Melissa Maker shares her best-kept hacks for your cleanest home yet.

item.title: Milan, Cortina Olympic cauldrons extinguished bringing end to Winter Games
item.description: A total of 116 medal events have been held in eight Olympic sports across 16 disciplines, including the debut of ski mountaineering this year.

item.title: Big first period helps London Knights knock off Sudbury Wolves 4-2
item.description: The London Knights scored four times in the first period on their way to a 4-2 victory over the Sudbury Wolves on Sunday at Canada Life Place.

item.description: The Canada Border Services Agency also confirmed in an email the connection between the suspension and the U.S. partial government shutdown.

item.title: Saskatoon’s hospitality industry trains to prevent human trafficking
item.description: Sunday marked National Human Trafficking Awareness Day. Saskatoon’s hospitality industry is working hard to protect those who may be exploited, with some help from Paul Brandt.

item.title: Calgary couple hopeful wedding dress and wheelchair will be returned after car theft
item.description: A Calgary family is hoping thieves will return a wedding dress and wheelchair that were in their car when it was stolen from outside a local business last week.
